title: Positive solutions of the explicit formula for ζ(s): near-criticality and uniqueness
description:
Paper (42 pages) with its LaTeX sources and ancillary files (certificate scripts, parameter files and logs), together with a companion manuscript and three notes from the same project. Preprint, October 2026; not yet peer-reviewed.

We study the positive solutions of Weil's explicit formula with the archimedean data of the Riemann zeta function: pairs of positive measures, one on the zero side and one on the prime side beyond log 2/(2π). By linear-programming duality such pairs exist if and only if a positivity statement involving neither zeros nor primes holds; its slack κ* gives the optimal degree-one explicit-formula conductor bound qmin = exp(−2πκ*). We conjecture that ζ's own pair is the only solution; this does not imply the Riemann hypothesis, but makes it equivalent to existence. We prove the conjecture for pairs carried by the zeros of ζ plus finitely many points and by the Bondarenko–Radchenko–Seip nodes, using positivity of the prime measure only on one residue class of nodes, and of the zero measure only at the origin. Certificates of the form Ξ2(H + ε·exp(−πt2)), with H a polynomial in t2, vanish at every zero of ζ and show unconditionally that κ* ≤ 1.1508391·10−906. Uniqueness would follow from asymptotic properties of a family of such functions, defined by Hermite interpolation at the prime powers.

The mathematics, proofs and text were produced by AI agents (Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5) under the author's direction; see the paper's AI-use statement.
